title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-20
ranking_basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains, descending.
ranking_explanation: Captured GitHub Trending?since=daily, corroborated against REST repository and default-branch commit endpoints, deduplicated by owner/name, filtered for forks, and sorted by displayed daily star gain. Includes the 12 highest-gain non-fork entries among 16 visible cards.
global_caveat: Point-in-time capture at 2026-11-20 01:40 UTC; Trending can change during the day. The newly-created repository Search query was noisy and was not used for ranking.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-20 01:40 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-20 through 2026-11-20. Ranking: daily Trending star gains, descending.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Today’s front page is led by reusable coding-agent workflows and skills, with strong adjacent demand for agent-ready software interfaces and web-context infrastructure. A smaller but visible counter-signal is continued interest in inference tooling and accessible small-model training.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Led today’s Trending star-gain signal by a wide margin, pointing to demand for structured, reusable agent workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: Latest push predates today’s surge; Trending measures attention, not release activity.

sections.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
sections.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain and a security-focused example of agent skills becoming packaged domain workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: README lists 83 skills and 433 individually cited patterns out of 681, while the Trending card says 82 skills; counts are project claims and efficacy was not independently audited.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: An agent skill that researches across social, video, community, prediction-market, and web sources, then synthesizes a grounded brief.
sections.why_notable: Third-highest gain; exemplifies agent-driven research combining fragmented public signals.
sections.unique_caveat: Available sources depend on configured credentials, tools, and opt-ins.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: A toolkit and community hub for making existing software agent-native through generated command-line interfaces.
sections.why_notable: A strong gain and a representative bet on giving agents structured CLI access to existing applications.
sections.unique_caveat: A software interoperability layer, not a general-purpose autonomous agent.

sections.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
sections.description: Web data infrastructure for agents: search, scrape, crawl, and access data providers through APIs.
sections.why_notable: High daily gain and a mature example of retrieval and web-ingestion infrastructure for agent applications.
sections.unique_caveat: README distinguishes local processing from cloud features; some workflows can use hosted services.

sections.title: cursor/plugins
sections.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins.
sections.why_notable: Signals that coding-agent ecosystems are formalizing plugin interfaces and curated integrations.

sections.title: mjmirza/app-store-compliance
sections.description: An open playbook and pre-submission guard for App Store and Google Play rejections, with policy checks and an agent skill.
sections.why_notable: Puts practical release and policy-compliance checks among today’s rising agent-adjacent workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: Verify policy advice against current official rules; listed rejection/deadline counts are project claims.

sections.title: XiaoYouChR/Ghost-Downloader-3
sections.description: A desktop download manager presented as an all-in-one downloader.
sections.why_notable: A higher-ranked non-agent utility, providing a counterpoint to the otherwise agent-centric front page.
sections.unique_caveat: The description is brief; this report makes no detailed claims about supported protocols or security.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: Agent Skills for the Stitch MCP server, intended for use across compatible coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Shows design tooling adopting portable skill packages and MCP-connected workflows.

sections.title: cathrynlavery/diagram-design
sections.description: Editorial diagram designs for coding agents, producing self-contained HTML and SVG.
sections.why_notable: A design-focused entry packaging visual conventions as reusable agent-facing instructions and outputs.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated 45 diagram types are from the repository description and were not individually evaluated.

sections.title: openvinotoolkit/openvino
sections.description: An open-source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference.
sections.why_notable: Brings established inference optimization infrastructure into a daily list led by agent workflows.

sections.title: jingyaogong/minimind
sections.description: An educational project for training a 64-million-parameter language model from scratch.
sections.why_notable: A hands-on model-training counterpoint making small-scale training approachable alongside production inference projects.
sections.unique_caveat: The two-hour claim depends on hardware and setup; it is not a runtime guarantee.

sections.content: Agent workflows and extension surfaces; web and social context; inference and small-scale model work; design tooling becoming agent-addressable. Languages: Python 5, TypeScript 3, Shell 2, HTML 1, C++ 1.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The clearest signal is not simply “more agents,” but the growth of the surrounding workflow layer: skills, plugins, app-specific CLIs, and retrieval tooling that connect agents to software and information. Today’s leaders coexist with mature inference infrastructure and smaller practical learning projects, suggesting continued demand across both application and model layers.

sections.title: Sources and Method

Daily gains are the figures displayed by the matching Trending view; GitHub REST verified totals, languages, status, push timestamps, and commit SHAs.
